title: Construction and formula of the canonical tame character
statement: For a strictly henselian DVR R, fraction field K, separable closure E⊆Ω with Ω algebraically closed, and residue characteristic exponent p, there exists a continuous surjective homomorphism t:Gal(E/K)→lim_(d,p)=1 μ_d(Ω). For every uniformizer π there is a compatible radical family α_d^d=π, and for every such π and family the coordinate formula is t(h)_d=h(α_d)/α_d. The topology and the compatibility equations are exactly those of [def-per-tame-root-limit].

source.place: Tags 0BUA and 0BUB; uniformizer radicals and tame kernel; compare ILO Expose XVII section 1.2, printed page 259.

proof.text: Every tame order is a unit in R and nonzero in E. The finite root sets of X^d-π with power transitions form a nonempty finite inverse system over the directed divisibility preorder. Finite inverse-system compactness supplies compatible radicals.

Take the finite canonical Kummer characters. Their formulas and radical compatibility show that they obey all power transitions, so they assemble into the tame limit subgroup. Coordinate continuity gives continuity into its defined initial topology.

For any target family, a finite-coordinate fiber in the compact absolute Galois group is closed and nonempty by finite character surjectivity. A product order refines two fibers, so compactness gives a common lift. The finite formula supplies uniformizer and root-choice independence.

theorem canonical_tame_character_data
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (Ksep : Type w) [Field Ksep] [Algebra K Ksep] [IsSepClosure K Ksep]
    (Ω : Type z) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra Ksep Ω]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p = if ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) = 0 then 1
      else ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)) :
    ∃ t : Gal(Ksep/K) →* TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p,
      @Continuous _ _ inferInstance (TameRoots.limitTopology Ω p) t ∧
      Function.Surjective t ∧
      (∀ π : R, Irreducible π →
        ∃ α : TameRoots.Order p → Ksep,
          (∀ d : TameRoots.Order p,
            α d ^ d.1 = algebraMap K Ksep (algebraMap R K π)) ∧
          ∀ d e : TameRoots.Order p, d.1 ∣ e.1 → α e ^ (e.1 / d.1) = α d) ∧
      (∀ (π : R), Irreducible π → ∀ α : TameRoots.Order p → Ksep,
        (∀ d : TameRoots.Order p,
          α d ^ d.1 = algebraMap K Ksep (algebraMap R K π)) →
        (∀ d e : TameRoots.Order p, d.1 ∣ e.1 → α e ^ (e.1 / d.1) = α d) →
        ∀ (h : Gal(Ksep/K)) (d : TameRoots.Order p),
          (((t h).1 d : Ωˣ) : Ω) = algebraMap Ksep Ω (h (α d) / α d))
